title: ProbeBench: trace seeding and regression diary
content:
Purpose:

This doc captures the current design and operational notes for ProbeBench — the microprobe-style benchmarking harness we use to (1) seed realistic request traces, (2) run targeted kernel sampling experiments, and (3) maintain a lightweight regression diary for performance surprises affecting the serving runtime. This is an engineering working doc: notes, hypotheses, reproducible steps and quick triage logs live here.

Background and motivation:

- We have multiple regression classes that are hard to catch with aggregate e2e tests: kernel performance shifts for long key-value (KV) cache hits, scheduler path contention at mid-batch sizes, and model-variant-induced latency cliffs for small tokens.
- Existing full-e2e trace replays are heavy and slow; ProbeBench is meant to be fast (minutes per experiment), deterministic where possible, and able to seed both synthetic and sampled real traces.
- Key goal: create a cheap guardrail that flags plausible regressions and provides reproducible microbench artifacts for root cause investigation.

High-level architecture:

1) Trace Seeder (probe-seeder):
   - Inputs: trace seed file (synthetic generator params OR sampled trace chunk), injection profile (arrival distribution, token length dist, conversation-turn probability), and target model variant.
   - Outputs: compact replayable trace (ndjson) annotated with KV context markers and optional kernel-capture hooks.
   - Modes: "fast-scan" (low-fidelity, high-speed), "fidelity" (replays prefix/KV cache warmup to match long-tail scenarios).

2) Probe Runner (probe-runner):
   - Runs trace files against a local or staging serving runtime.
   - Configurable options: concurrency, batch size distribution, sequence length cap, kv-warmup rounds, kernel sampling frequency.
   - Produces per-request telemetry and aggregated micrometrics (per-token timing, KV hit/miss latency, GPU kernel durations when sampled).

3) Kernel Sampler (sampler-daemon):
   - Lightweight sampler integrated with the runtime's kernel scheduler.
   - On configured intervals picks N in-flight requests and records kernel-level timing for attention, matmul-ish ops, kv-cache lookup & insert, and memory copy (H2D/D2H).
   - Output: compact kernel sample records that map back to trace request ids.

4) Regression Detector (probe-alert):
   - Offline process comparing baseline metric snapshots to new-run snapshots.
   - Metrics: median latency per token, p95/p99 token tail, kv-hit latency distribution, kernel hotpaths median and 95th, throughput @ 99th perc concurrency, flakiness score (variance over runs).
   - Rules: threshold-based rules for obvious breaches + anomaly scoring using EWMA on p95 with configurable sensitivity.

Trace seeding strategies and examples:

- Synthetic conversational seeds: mixture of short-turn (<16 tokens) and long-turn (>128 tokens) with reply branching (simulate multi-turn chat). Useful to exercise kernel dispatch and KV cache churn.
- Sampled real traces: take 10–20s sliding windows from production trace-sampler (obfuscate content) and replay with reduced request rate but identical token lengths/turn structure to preserve KV locality.
- Focused KV experiments: generate seeds with high prefix reuse across sessions to stress the cache and validate eviction heuristics.

Key microbench scenarios (examples we run daily/weekly):

- Tiny-token throughput sweep: batches of 1–8 tokens per request at high concurrency to exercise scheduler path overhead and microkernel launch cost.
- KV-heavy tail: 80% cache hits, 20% cold prefix inserts with variable sequence lengths (to observe miss latencies and eviction timing).
- Kernel-shop experiment: run with kernel sampling on/off to evaluate sampler overhead and measure attention vs matmul ratios across model variants.
- Mixed workload: 70% generation, 20% embedding invites, 10% reranking calls (different backend code paths) to validate cross-route isolation and shared GPU contention.

Regression detection heuristics and actionable thresholds (starting defaults):

- Token median latency regression: raise if new_med >= baseline_med * 1.18 AND delta_abs >= 0.6ms.
- P95 token latency: alert if new_p95 >= baseline_p95 + 5ms OR relative increase > 20%.
- Kernel hotpath shift: if sampled kernel A's median increases > 25% and contributes >10% of total token time, mark for probe.
- KV-hit tail: if p99 of kv-hit latency grows > 2x or exceeds 8ms.
- Flakiness: if standard deviation across 5 runs increases > 30% vs baseline.

Operational playbook (triage steps):

1) Run ProbeBench with the same seed and configuration three times to confirm reproducibility. Use --attach-kernel-samples where available.
2) If regression is reproduced: collect kernel samples and full runtime trace (short window around offending requests).
3) Narrow by toggling KV warmup and batch-size distribution to see which axis reduces the regression.
4) If kernel sample implicates a specific op, capture a microkernel profile (nvprof/similar) on a controlled node.
5) Open issue and tag owners: runtime-kernels, scheduler, kv-cache. Attach ProbeBench artifacts and a short reproduction script.

Recent diary entries (quick log of investigations):

- 2024-12-04 -- p95 regressions observed on nightly for small-token throughput. Reproduced locally using probe-seeder fast-scan. Root cause: scheduler changed default spin yield behavior in PR 3890. Mitigation: revert yield tweak + add unit test. Owner: Marco.
- 2024-12-18 -- KV-hit p99 spike on longer conversations in dedicated pool test. Trace seeding with high prefix reuse reproduced. Kernel samples showed occasional heavy memcpy at eviction path. Hypothesis: new slab allocator alignment increased copy cost. Owner: Priya. Action: add targeted allocator microbench and slower rollout.
- 2025-01-03 -- flakiness increase in kernel sampler itself (sampler added 1.2ms median overhead on some GPUs). Temporary reduction of sampler frequency and added low-overhead sampling mode. Owner: Ethan.

Repro steps for a new investigator (quick):

1) checkout serving-runtime branch probebench-experiments.
2) export PROBEBENCH_CONFIG=/tmp/probe.yml (example config attached in repo).
3) run: ./tools/probe-runner --seed traces/kv-heavy-sample.ndjson --runs 3 --concurrency 32 --kv-warmup 5 --attach-kernel-samples
4) Wait for artifacts in /tmp/probe-output/<timestamp> (summary.json, kernel-samples.ndjson, perf-flame.svg).
5) Compare summary.json to baseline snapshots in artifacts/baselines/ using tools/probe-compare.

Open questions / TODOs:

- Better synthetic generator: need to capture inter-request semantics that drive KV locality across user sessions (we currently stitch simple prefixes). Design task: user-affinity model in seeder. Owner: Asha.
- Add deterministic seeded-mode for GPU kernels to reduce nondeterminism in sampler results. Research required on interplay with allocator and CUDA stream parallelism. Owner: Ravi.
- Integrate with CI gating: define cheap ProbeBench smoke that runs on every release candidate (30s run) and gates merge on high-sensitivity rules. Owner: Marco + SRE.
- Formalize baseline snapshots per model-variant and per-hardware-class (A10 vs H100 priors). Right now baselines are ad-hoc. Owner: Priya.

Artifacts and where to look:

- Repo: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime (tools/probe-*)
- Probe outputs archived in s3://redwood-probebench/artifacts/ (folders named by run id).
- Kernel sampler proto: docs in confluence://page/serving-runtime/kernel-sampler-proto

Notes to self (quick):

- Keep per-run seed id in metadata so we can correlate trace-seeder config with prod-sample id.
- When trying to reproduce p95 cliffs, prefer fidelity mode with KV warmup equal to observed session warmup length.
- Sampler should avoid heavy state mutation: prefer copy-on-write buffers for sample extraction.

Appendix: small checklist for adding a new ProbeBench experiment

- [ ] Define hypothesis and metric(s) to observe (latency quantiles + kernel share).
- [ ] Create or pick a trace seed (synthetic vs sampled) and document rationale.
- [ ] Run baseline 5x to capture noise floor.
- [ ] Run experiment 5x with kernel sampling on and off.
- [ ] Collect artifacts, tag with run metadata, and open issue if regression persists.

End of working diary.

(If you're reading this and want write access or to contribute seeds: ping me in #eng-serving-runtime or leave a note in the linked JIRA).
